correctness.rationale: In characteristic two a nondegenerate alternating form is symmetric, and the radical-cubed-zero product defines a commutative associative local Gorenstein algebra. All unital subalgebras are k plus a multiplication-closed radical subspace. Subspaces containing the one-dimensional radical square are automatically closed; disjoint ones are graphs over totally isotropic spaces, and unrestricted central shears act freely/transitively on their graph parameters. The automorphism group is exactly the symplectic similitude group with all central shears. Witt extension classifies the containing-socle pieces by (dim radical of restricted form, half its rank) and the disjoint-socle pieces by isotropic dimension. The polar flag product and symplectic group quotient count each orbit. Independent RREF enumeration and generated-group orbit traversal checked all q=2,4,8 cases for m=1, both q=2,4 for m=2, and q=2 for m=3. These experiments are not used to prove infinite m/e.

originality.rationale: The claimed contribution is the complete ring-subalgebra orbit and cardinality spectrum of the symplectic characteristic-two short local Gorenstein family, including all nonideal isotropic graph fibers. The closest Gorenstein classification source studies isomorphism classes, not embedded unital subalgebras; the closest finite classical-space source classifies subspace types, not which are multiplication-closed in these algebras. The classical transitivity and counting input is explicitly acknowledged, and the result is not claimed as a new symplectic theorem. Specific searches found no identical finite-ring classification; residual risk of differently titled ring/subring enumeration and indirect implication from combined existing tools remains.

value.rationale: A complete, intrinsically motivated all-m subalgebra-lattice orbit invariant for finite characteristic-two short Gorenstein local rings: every stratum and its size is specified, as are the dimension generating polynomial and exact difference from ideals. For m>=2 the symplectic-radical strata have nontrivial ranks and orbit sizes, and the additional isotropic graph strata can dominate the count. The result is not merely an isolated finite-case table or numerical substitution; it gives a structural classification of a natural infinite family. It does not claim a further theorem or downstream applications not proved.
